question: The average price of three items of furniture is ₹15,135. If their prices are in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7, the price of the cheapest item (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio parts = 3 + 5 + 7 = 15.

Total price = Average × 3 = 15135 × 3.

Cheapest item corresponds to 3 parts out of 15, which is exactly 1/5 of the **total price**.

Price of cheapest item = (15135 × 3) ÷ 5 = 3027 × 3 = 9081.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,081.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average price** of 3 items = ₹15,135

**Ratio** of prices = 3 : 5 : 7

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = **Average** × Number of items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/613830d27e15dd8da37916c538e3dc9f9eb9aff597aaf48a089221cc919bd92f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total price of 3 furniture items = 15,135 × 3 = ₹45,405

⇒ Sum of the **ratio units** = 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 units

⇒ 15 units = ₹45,405

⇒ 1 unit = 45,405 ÷ 15

⇒ 1 unit = ₹3,027

⇒ Price of the **cheapest item** (3 units) = 3 × 3,027

⇒ Price of the cheapest item = ₹9,081

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,081.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Distribution Rule

If a value V is divided in the ratio a : b : c, then the value of the smallest part is [a ÷ (a + b + c)] × V.

Average Relationship

Average = Sum of values ÷ Total number of values. Thus, Sum = Average × Count.

Common Ratio Multiplier

Multiplying the simplified ratio (3:5:7) by a common factor (k = ₹3,027) gives the actual individual values.
